decisions.flow_scope_and_granularity: End-to-end user-system behavior – One user interaction followed by one system response
decisions.structure_exploration_depth: Behavioral -> Explore business and behavioral AC (user interactions, workflows, outcomes)

rationale.depth_of_shaping: Authentication is a well-established pattern (CRUD + security). Implementation is complete and testable. Minimal examples are sufficient (registration, login, protected route). No need for extensive scenario decomposition as patterns are standard.
rationale.drill_down_approach: User authentication workflows are critical (register → login → use). Security is highest value area (password hashing, JWT tokens). System interactions are standard (REST API patterns). Architectural pieces are well-established (JWT, bcrypt).
rationale.drill_down_limits: Authentication is a focused capability with clear boundaries: User Registration, User Login, Token Verification, Protected Route Access, User Info Retrieval. These 5 stories cover the complete authentication flow. No need for extensive decomposition.
rationale.flow_scope_and_granularity: Authentication follows clear request-response patterns: User registers → System creates user, User logs in → System returns token, User requests protected resource → System validates token → System returns resource. Each interaction is atomic and well-defined. Journey-level documentation would be overkill for this focused capability.
rationale.structure_exploration_depth: Authentication is primarily behavioral (user actions and system responses). Structural elements (User model, token structure) are simple and well-defined. Focus should be on user interactions: registration flow, login flow, token usage. Outcomes are clear: successful registration, successful login, protected access.

accepted: Focus on user flow over internal systems - Implementation focuses on user-facing endpoints (register, login, me) rather than internal system details
Cover the end-to-end scenario - Implementation covers complete authentication flow: registration → login → token usage → protected resource access
Prioritize customer-facing features - All endpoints are customer-facing (register, login, user info). No internal-only endpoints
Assume stories should be independently testable - Each component (login, registration, middleware) is independently testable. Tests exist for each module
Assume each story delivers user value - Each feature (registration, login, protected routes) delivers direct user value
Skip deep drill-down where patterns are well-established - Standard CRUD operations, familiar workflows, proven integration patterns can stay high-level

modified.assumption: Assume technical infrastructure stories are implicit
modified.modification: While infrastructure is implemented, the repository pattern explicitly acknowledges future database needs. This suggests we should document the infrastructure replacement story as a future enhancement.

implementation_status.note: All required functionality for secure user authentication with JWT tokens has been implemented, tested, and documented. The system is ready for production use (after setting proper JWT_SECRET_KEY environment variable).

future_considerations: Database integration (repository pattern already supports this)
